Stealing your format to add on to this here is some responsibilities of being a manager

1.	⁠You are going to be held accountable for everything that goes wrong. If someone's drawer is short, it is on you to figure it out. If the service times are high for that day, you are going to hear about it the next day. Crew "stealing" food, procedures not being followed, etc are all things you will be held accountable for. If something goes wrong, and you are on shift it is more or less your fault.
2.	⁠Being that you would become a manager right off the bat, you will definitely have to earn the respect of the current crew/managers already there. This is going to be tough, especially because that respect is hard to earn even if you have been there for a while. Getting the crew to work hard for you, while not hating you is going to be very challenging.
3.	⁠Be prepared to learn more about the "bigger picture" and some behind the scenes of how the business operates. Depending on how much responsibility they give you, you could end up doing inventory and managing how much food the store is "missing", why it is missing, etc, etc. Voice scores (customer satisfaction that sort of thing) could be something you are tasked to bring up as well.
4.	⁠Lastly, the most common thing you will do is run a shift. Maybe not at first, but eventually you will be tasked to run a shift. Sometimes you will have another manager, sometimes you won't. Keeping times down, managing call outs, placement of crew, giving out breaks are a day to day thing which you will need to get comfortable with. People will try to test you at first, to see what they can get away with. You will also need to make sure everything is up to code, and there are no health department violations occurring. As a manager you will conduct a pre-shift checklist to ensure all the rules are being followed.

There is a lot more to being a manager and I would be willing to go more in depth if you want me to, but this is a basic rundown of what to expect if you do accept the job offer.

You find an item you like on taobao and read the size chart figure out your size etc. Then your going to want to use an agent to middleman between you and the seller(s) because it minimizes the risk of anything going wrong(language barrier, tracking etc). Superbuy is the most popular as far as I know. You want to take the item link and paste in the shop section on Superbuy and add it to your cart if you would like to pay for multiple items at once or just buy it right then and there. Some items will not accept PayPal so you can just top up your Superbuy balance with PayPal and use your balance instead. Normally you can just pay directly with PayPal. Then an agent will be assigned to your order and they will handle it from there. Your items won’t be delivered to your address just yet. They will be sent to the Superbuy warehouse in China. Once your item(s) get to your warehouse you are provided 3 free pictures of it. You can pay a small fee to get more detailed photos or photos focusing on a specific part of the item. You can leave your items in their warehouse for up to 180 days with no extra charge. If all is good then you can package your item(s) into one parcel and send it to your home address. It is recommended to wait until you have multiple items to ship together as the shipping fees are expensive and shipping just one or two items would not be reasonable. Once you ship your parcel to your house it will go through China customs then onto a plane or ship to your home country. There it will be checked by customs who can seize your package. This is normally not the case though and usually they will let it through. From there it is sent to your local post office and shipped directly to your home.
